project.name: FreeType
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO container checkout at `/src/freetype2` is on commit `db17ceb4c0a9acb307c033fb766c8f35ac9e007f`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `ft_var_load_hvar` logic shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42499092 (freetype2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target ftfuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42499092
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is an OpenType/CFF2 variable font whose `fvar` table declares 2 variation axes while its `HVAR` item variation store declares 34 axes. During `setIntermediateAxis(face)`, FreeType first reads the `fvar` header, materializes `fvar_head.axisCount = 2`, copies that value into `mmvar->num_axis`, and `TT_Set_MM_Blend` allocates `blend->normalizedcoords` for exactly those two axes. Later, when glyph loading reaches `tt_face_get_metrics` and `tt_hadvance_adjust`, FreeType lazily parses `HVAR`, accepts `itemStore->axisCount = 34` without checking it against the earlier `fvar` count, and builds 34-axis region records plus a width map with 312 covered glyphs, all selecting `varData[0]`. That `varData[0]` record carries `regionIdxCount = 5` and `regionIndices = [0,1,2,3,4]`, so the first master iteration selects `varRegionList[0].axisList` and the inner loop runs `j < itemStore.axisCount`. Once `j` reaches 2, the comparison at `ttgxvar.c:851` reads past the 2-entry `normalizedcoords` allocation, producing the observed AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8`. The fix adds the missing `itemStore->axisCount != (FT_Long)blend->mmvar->num_axis` rejection in `ft_var_load_hvar`.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled `fvar` bytes and materializes `fvar_head.axisCount`, the field later copied into blend metadata and used to size variation allocations.
source.value_from: Static inspection of `gt_results/arvo_42499092/poc` shows the `fvar` header declares `axisCount == 2`. `TT_Get_MM_Var` reads that header here before any later copy into `mmvar->num_axis` and before `TT_Set_MM_Blend` allocates `blend->normalizedcoords`.

sink.code: else if ( face->blend->normalizedcoords[j] < axis->startCoord || face->blend->normalizedcoords[j] > axis->endCoord )
sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The HVAR per-axis comparison reads `normalizedcoords[j]` using the larger HVAR axis count even though `normalizedcoords` was allocated for only the smaller `fvar` axis count.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8` at `ttgxvar.c:851:19`, 0 bytes after a 16-byte region allocated by `TT_Set_MM_Blend`.

root_cause.description: Missing HVAR-vs-fvar axis-count validation. After reading `itemStore->axisCount`, the vulnerable parser does not reject a mismatch against `blend->mmvar->num_axis`; the fix adds that exact check immediately after this read.
root_cause.note: In the saved witness, `itemStore->axisCount == 34` while the earlier `fvar` state from `TT_Get_MM_Var` is `blend->mmvar->num_axis == 2`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The out-of-bounds loop bound originates when `ft_var_load_hvar` reads the HVAR region-axis count from the attacker-controlled font. Static parsing of `gt_results/arvo_42499092/poc` shows this field is 34.

parser_admitted.code: if ( FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates( face, FT_UInt( coords.size() ), coords.data() ) )
parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted to FreeType's variable-font path here. `setIntermediateAxis` first calls `FT_Get_MM_Var(face, &variations_ptr)`, which executes the scored `fvar` read, then it calls `FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates`, which reaches `TT_Set_MM_Blend` and allocates `face->blend->normalizedcoords` before glyph loading begins.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness recognizes the witness as a variable OpenType/CFF2 face, calls `FT_Get_MM_Var` to read the `fvar` table, then calls `FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates` to build variation state before loading glyphs.

FreeType reads `fvar.axisCount == 2` into `fvar_head`, copies it into `mmvar->num_axis`, and `TT_Set_MM_Blend` allocates `blend->normalizedcoords` for exactly two axes; ASan later attributes the overflowing heap region to this allocation.

On first HVAR use, `ft_var_load_hvar` reads `itemStore.axisCount == 34` and `regionCount == 5` from the witness's `HVAR` table, builds 34-axis region records, parses `varData[0]` with `regionIdxCount == 5` and `regionIndices == [0,1,2,3,4]`, and stores a 312-entry width map whose entries all select `outerIndex == 0`.

During glyph loading, `tt_hadvance_adjust` takes a glyph covered by the width map, resolves it to `varData[0]`, selects `regionIndex == 0` on the first master iteration, and then iterates 34 axes against the 2-entry `normalizedcoords` allocation until line 851 overreads it.

fine_trace.note: Source. `TT_Get_MM_Var` reads the attacker-controlled `fvar` header from the stream into `fvar_head`; static inspection of the saved witness shows this materializes `fvar_head.axisCount == 2`.
`TT_Get_MM_Var` copies the parsed `fvar` axis count from step 1 into `mmvar->num_axis`. This smaller count becomes the blend-side axis cardinality used by later allocations and consistency checks.

During `setIntermediateAxis(face)` -> `FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates` -> `TT_Set_MM_Blend`, FreeType allocates `blend->normalizedcoords` using the smaller count from step 2. The saved ASan allocation stack points here and reports a 16-byte region, consistent with two `FT_Fixed` slots on this build.

Root cause. The HVAR parser reads the witness's region-axis count and stores `itemStore->axisCount == 34` and `regionCount == 5`, but it does not reject the mismatch against `blend->mmvar->num_axis == 2` from step 2. The fix adds that exact comparison immediately after this read.

Because step 4's larger count is accepted, each HVAR region allocates and records 34 axis descriptors. The witness has 5 regions, so every later `regionIndex` resolves to one of these 34-entry `axisList` records.

fine_trace.code:
if ( FT_READ_USHORT( hvarData->itemCount )      ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( shortDeltaCount )          ||
     FT_READ_USHORT( hvarData->regionIdxCount ) )
fine_trace.note: For `varData[0]`, this block materializes `itemCount == 118`, `regionIdxCount == 5`, and `regionIndices == [0,1,2,3,4]`. Any mapped glyph that later selects `outerIndex == 0` will therefore drive the master loop across five regions, beginning with region 0.

This width-map block stores `widthMap->mapCount == 312` and decodes 312 one-byte map entries. Static raw decode of the witness shows every stored entry yields `outerIndex == 0` and `innerIndex` between 0 and 117, so every covered glyph selects `varData[0]` and an in-range `deltaSet` row.

The crashing call necessarily passes the `gindex >= mapCount` guard, so its glyph index lies in the first 312 mapped glyphs. Stage 01 did not preserve the exact `gindex`, but step 7 makes the remaining ambiguity non-load-bearing: every covered glyph yields `outerIndex == 0`, so this statement always selects `varData[0]`; the glyph-specific `innerIndex` remains an in-range 0..117 value used only to choose `deltaSet`.

The per-region loop starts with `master == 0`. Because step 6 stored `regionIndices[0] == 0` and `regionIdxCount == 5`, the first iteration resolves `regionIndex == 0` and points `axis` at `varRegionList[0].axisList`, the first 34-entry region record from step 5.

The per-axis loop now iterates `j < itemStore.axisCount`, i.e. 34 times, across the chosen region's `axisList`. Nothing rechecks the earlier 2-axis `normalizedcoords` extent, so `j` can advance beyond the last valid normalized coordinate.

fine_trace.code:
else if ( face->blend->normalizedcoords[j] < axis->startCoord ||
          face->blend->normalizedcoords[j] > axis->endCoord   )
fine_trace.note: ASan sink. Once the loop reaches `j == 2`, this comparison reads `normalizedcoords[2]`, one element past the 2-entry heap allocation from step 3. The saved crash reports a `READ of size 8` at `ttgxvar.c:851:19`, 0 bytes after that 16-byte region.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack attributes the overflowing 16-byte heap region to `FT_NEW_ARRAY( blend->normalizedcoords, mmvar->num_axis )`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan frame 0 is `tt_hadvance_adjust` at `src/truetype/ttgxvar.c:851`, exactly the sink in step 11.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocation stack shows `TT_Set_MM_Blend` sizing `blend->normalizedcoords`, and the patch's missing HVAR-vs-fvar axis-count check is exactly what allows `tt_hadvance_adjust` to index beyond that allocation with `itemStore->axisCount`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The fine trace's vulnerable use in `tt_hadvance_adjust` is reached through the same `tt_face_get_metrics -> cff_slot_load -> FT_Load_Glyph` stack recorded in the saved crash, and the allocation side matches `TT_Set_Var_Design -> TT_Set_MM_Blend -> setIntermediateAxis`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness's `HVAR` field `itemStore->axisCount == 34` is stored at step 4, carried into 34-entry region records at step 5, paired with `varData[0]` and the 312-entry width map at steps 6-8, reused as the inner-loop bound at step 10, and makes step 11 read `normalizedcoords[j]` beyond the 2-entry allocation created from `fvar.axisCount == 2`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42499092-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed `poc` to `ftfuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` in `tt_hadvance_adjust` with stack `tt_face_get_metrics -> cff_slot_load`.

format.name: OpenType/CFF2 variable font
format.contract: Exactly the 242272-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42499092/poc` (sha256 `14266258e06363957816a84e992b40a97f6c8e42b99c86f002bbaad5c17dd950`). Static inspection of this file shows `fvar.axisCount == 2`, `HVAR` item-variation-store `axisCount == 34`, `regionCount == 5`, `varData[0].itemCount == 118`, `varData[0].regionIdxCount == 5`, `varData[0].regionIndices == [0,1,2,3,4]`, and `widthMap.mapCount == 312` with every stored width-map entry decoding to `outerIndex == 0` and `innerIndex` in `0..117`. In the staged harness, `setIntermediateAxis(face)` first reads `fvar.axisCount == 2` through `FT_Get_MM_Var`, then `FT_Set_Var_Design_Coordinates` allocates `blend->normalizedcoords` for those two `fvar` axes. Stage 01 did not preserve the exact crashing `gindex`, but that ambiguity is not load-bearing because any covered glyph selects `varData[0]`, the first master iteration chooses `regionIndex == 0`, and the unchecked 34-axis inner loop then reads past `normalizedcoords[2]`.
